plan: Trim SPY to 20% to reduce concentration and meet the mandate.
Sell QQQI and QQQ due to downtrends and for capital preservation.
Sell CRWD and SMH to reduce single name and sector exposure.
Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL) to zero for capital preservation.
This plan aims for a large cash buffer and tight stops.
conservative.read: This conservative plan targets around 1.5% per month, prioritizing capital preservation. It significantly reduces risk by cutting leveraged ETFs and high-beta names, but also limits upside potential. Expect lower drawdowns but also modest returns.

plan: Trim SPY to 25% to meet the concentration mandate.
Sell QQQI and QQQ due to their downtrends.
Trim SMH to 5% to reduce exposure to a downtrending sector.
Maintain small positions in SOXL and SPAL for limited leveraged exposure.
Buy SNOW at 10% as a strong scanner setup to diversify.
balanced.read: This balanced plan targets around 2.5% per month, focusing on risk-first growth. It blends broad index exposure with quality tech and limited leverage. Expect moderate drawdowns and growth potential.

plan: Trim SPY to 25% to meet the concentration mandate.
Sell QQQI and QQQ to reallocate capital from downtrends.
Trim SMH to 5% to reduce exposure to a downtrending sector.
Add to SOXL and SPAL to increase leveraged exposure.
Buy SNOW at 10% as a strong scanner setup for aggressive growth.
aggressive.read: This aggressive plan targets around 4% per month, aiming for stretched growth. It uses and adds leveraged ETFs, increasing both upside and drawdown potential. Be aware of daily decay and the potential for significant losses if stops are not strictly adhered to.

plan: Trim SPY to 20% to reduce concentration and meet the mandate.
Add to QQQI to 30% for increased income exposure.
Sell QQQ, CRWD, and SMH to reduce growth and high-beta exposure.
Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL) to zero.
This plan prioritizes steady monthly distributions and low drawdown.
income.read: This income plan targets around 1% per month, focusing on parking cash for yield. It prioritizes low drawdown and reliable income over growth, but distributions are variable and NAV can still fall. Expect steady income with limited growth potential.
